title: formpublisher

catalog.name: FormPublisher
catalog.summary: Open FormWeb sites, check every route, package them and prepare them for hosts.

notes_for_owner: The first formcompiler build of formpublisher. The release stays a draft on the private repository. The entry was drafted while the repository was blank and now follows it: the version is src-tauri/tauri.conf.json's, the check is ci.yml (it runs on pushes to main, so the compile branch's commit must be one that passed on main), and the licence is GPL-3.0-only as its LICENSE says. It builds in commands mode, not contract mode: ./formpublisher has no install-desktop command and ./build_app refuses --config, so formcompiler's Tauri settings reach the build through the tauri.<os>.conf.json it merges before every build. ./build_app keeps its Rust build folder in the user's cache unless FORMPUBLISHER_CARGO_TARGET is set, so the build points it at src-tauri/target, where the bundles are collected; on macOS --no-install stops it copying the app to Applications, and it packs the disk image itself after tauri build makes the app. Linux builds deb, AppImage and rpm, with rpm compression off as FormVis does. Windows runs build_app.bat under cmd, which writes everything to build_app.log, so the line prints that log when it fails. The install compiles a second Rust workspace, which adds minutes to every build. tauri build comes from npx @tauri-apps/cli@2 at build time, not from the app's lock file. updater.tauri is false: the app has no updater yet. mcp_launch is left out until the bundle carries form-app.json beside the engine. The Intel Mac build uses formcompiler's cryptography wheel, which is built for macOS 14, so an Intel Mac older than 14 may not run it although the app says macOS 13. The read token must be able to read nodemode-dev/formpublisher before this runs: the feed plan fails naming any enabled repository it cannot read.
